# Gelabber v0.5.0

Integrated through feature PR #170 into `v0.5` and the version PR into `main`.

## Desktop app for Linux (new)

- Native app for Linux x86_64, first for Arch/Omarchy with Hyprland/Wayland.
  It loads your own Gelabber server: login, chat and interface are the familiar
  web app, and the server address is asked for on first start.
- Media runs through a native core (libwebrtc + libmediasoupclient) instead of
  WebKitGTK: voice with all three microphone modes including local RNNoise and
  the microphone test, screen sharing through the desktop portal (PipeWire)
  with hardware H264 via NVENC/VA-API where available and VP8 otherwise,
  Go Live with the sound of a chosen application, camera, and streams in their
  own windows whose quality follows the window size.
- Installing on Arch: package `gelabber-desktop` from the signed pacman
  repository, then updates with `yay -Syu`
  (`desktop/packaging/arch/README.md`). Other distributions: unpack
  `gelabber-desktop-linux-x64.tar.gz` from this release.
- With the NVIDIA driver under Wayland, WebKitGTK runs without its DMA-BUF
  renderer.
- Windows follows in a later version.

## Web app

- Detects the desktop app and uses the native media path there; in browsers
  every path stays as in v0.4.0.

## Upgrade and operation

- No database migrations and no `.env` changes. API and media are unchanged
  in content since v0.4.0; the web image carries the app path. Still update or
  roll back the image set (`GELABBER_{API,WEB,MEDIA}_IMAGE`) together; going
  back to v0.4.0 touches no data.

## Open

- Acceptance of the desktop app on real NVIDIA and Intel hardware (screen
  sharing via NVENC/VA-API, real microphones and echo cancellation, a call over
  the internet through TURN) is still pending.
- The Linux package contains libwebrtc's H264 decoder (FFmpeg); the licensing
  question is not finally settled.
